matrix_metadata.derivation_rule: Expected behaviour is derived from cases.json, supplied evidence, and the source Reason Codes PDF. Existing persisted recommendations are not treated as authority.

rules: Relevant or persuasive evidence is not qualifying evidence unless it establishes an encoded source-derived route.
Model confidence and merchant confidence never bind to policy predicates.
Suggested analyst action is separate from recommendation.
All evidence citations use the original source filename and one-based page number; images use page 1.
Invalid extraction produces no partial downstream result.

expected_qualifying_facts: The listing describes a Carlton armchair with sage velvet upholstery.
The image caption states Carlton Armchair (Sage), delivered 18 April 2025.
The visible image appears to show a sage-green armchair.
The caption states the photo is a front view only.
The general returns policy describes return and defective-item routes.
relevant_but_insufficient_evidence: Visible type and colour support a limited visible-attribute comparison.
The front-view image cannot address the claimed wobble or hidden structural fault.
The general return policy does not show whether this cardholder requested, used, refused or completed a return process.
deliberate_ambiguity: The photograph does not expose the chair's structural stability.
No case-specific return correspondence or inspection is supplied.
facts_that_must_not_be_inferred: The chair does not wobble.
No hidden structural defect exists.
The chair is defect-free.
Every product feature matches the listing.
The customer completed, refused or failed to use a valid return route.
No visible damage means no damage exists.

expected_requirement_outcomes.basis: The product listing supplies a published description.
Type and colour visibly align, but the front-view image cannot establish material condition or the alleged structural defect.

expected_requirement_outcomes.description: Unused return route or post-complaint use and retention
expected_requirement_outcomes.basis: A general return route is documented, but neither alternative has case-specific evidence.

missing_evidence: A case-specific inspection or multi-angle evidence addressing the alleged structural fault.
Case-specific return/refund correspondence and return-request search records.
Evidence of post-complaint use and retention if relying on that alternative route.

requested_items: Request a case-specific inspection or evidence addressing the alleged wobble/leg seating.
Request return correspondence and merchant records showing whether a return route was offered and used.
Alternatively request evidence of post-complaint use and retention.

required_citations.supports: Caption text, visible armchair, sage-green appearance and front-view limitation.

expected_qualifying_facts: Booking MSP-2025-4488 for 26 to 27 April 2025.
Non-refundable 215 EUR rate.

Front-desk log records NO-SHOW at 00:30 on 27 April 2025.
The policy applies the full charge to no-show.

deliberate_ambiguity: No cancellation timestamp is supplied, so the late-cancellation alternative is not evaluated for this case; the independently sufficient NO-SHOW route is established.
facts_that_must_not_be_inferred: No cancellation occurred merely because no cancellation record is supplied.
The model decides whether a cancellation was late.
A date-only value is silently treated as a precise timestamp.

expected_requirement_outcomes.basis: The booking confirmation identifies the reservation and service dates.
The accepted policy records disclosure and tick-box consent.
The front-desk log records exact status NO-SHOW.
The booking amount is 215 EUR and the accepted policy makes the full amount non-refundable for no-show.

required_citations.supports: Policy disclosure, consent and full-charge no-show rule.
